summary: Nvidia is the central node of the entire AI ecosystem and its competitive moat is the financability of its data centers plus locked-up supply chain
summary_extended: Baker argues that Nvidia is the central node of the entire AI ecosystem, with its competitive moat rooted not just in chip performance but in the superior financeability of its data centers and its stranglehold on the global AI supply chain. Specifically, Nvidia has locked up approximately 70-80% of world compute supply across fab capacity, DRAM, NAND, lasers, capacitors, and rack components, making it structurally irreplaceable in the near term. The financing advantage is decisive: a $50B Nvidia data center requires only $15B in equity with the remaining $35B financed at low rates via residual value guarantees (RVGs), whereas TPU-based alternatives require roughly double the equity at higher rates, dramatically raising the cost of competing. Jensen Huang's strategy of being vertically integrated but horizontally open — spanning nine chip types, land, power, shell companies, and offtake matchmaking — further entrenches Nvidia's position while RVGs democratize access for non-hyperscaler AI labs, aligning Nvidia's dominance with US national interest. Baker explicitly states that 26 years of experience have taught him not to bet against Jensen, framing NVDA as a high-conviction long with a structural, long-duration moat in AI infrastructure financing.
